speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you've ruled out fever and infection, have you noticed any involuntary eye movements, such as a jerking motion to one side (nystagmus), or difficulty pointing your fingers quickly? Also, do you have a personal or family history of similar neurological issues, or any known exposure to toxins like heavy metals or certain medications?

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Spinocerebellar Ataxia (likely autosomal dominant hereditary ataxia).

The absence of acute fever, infection, or sudden onset like a stroke, combined with progressive gait and limb ataxia affecting the right side, strongly points toward a neurodegenerative condition rather than an acute lesion. We will proceed with genetic testing and a detailed neurological exam once the MRI results are reviewed to confirm this.
